structs.name: bitarray_224
structs.size_evidence: method 3 (whole-object write): Com_Teams_GetEnemyTeamFlags@0x140E642F0 writes outFlags as a qword at 0, a qword at 8 and a dword at 16 (= 20 bytes), copying the 20-byte mask from StaticMask160_Get_70000000@0x1410D5250 / StaticMask160_GetAllSet@0x1410D51D0 (OWORD + dword). Whole-object clears: memset(&teamFlags, 0, 20) in Sentient_Init@0x1411E5480 and Sentient_UpdateNavObstaclesForTeam@0x1411E5EE0. Readers stop at word 4: Path_NodePassesTeamRepulsorTest@0x1411CA690 reads *teamFlags (words 0-3) and teamFlags[1].m128i_i32[0] (word 4) only; Actor_BroadcastAgentEvent@0x1411B2EB0 loops 5 words (v8 < 5). No function read touches word 5 or 6.
members: Nav_GetObstacleBlockageFlagsFromTeamFlags@0x140FFFE80 and Nav_TranslateTeamFlagsToRepulsorUsageFlags@0x1410040C0 read array[0] (CONFIRMED); Com_Teams_GetEnemyTeamFlags@0x140E642F0 clears and writes array[4] with &= ~0x10 and &= 0xFFFFFF9F (CONFIRMED, word 4 is the last word); Actor_BroadcastAgentEvent reads array[0..4] (CONFIRMED)
changed_members: method 3 above; StaticMask160 is the 5-word mask all team sets are copied from
unconfirmed: the type name: Replay's team mask is 160 bits (StaticMask160, 5 words); no 224-bit object exists in Replay. Suggest the type be called bitarray_160 (not in renames: a type rename is the coordinator's call)
structs.notes: Game-test bitarray<224> has 7 words; Replay's team-flag object is 5 words everywhere it is built or read (Sentient_Init and Sentient_UpdateNavObstaclesForTeam clear 20 bytes, Actor_BroadcastAgentEvent loops 5 words, Com_Teams writes 20 bytes). The struct is used by pointer and by value only as a 20-byte stack local, and bitarray_160 / bitarray_192 exist in the IDA local types only as unused names. Team index limit: Actor_EventListener_First/Next index array[eTeam >> 5], so eTeam must stay below 160 in Replay (consistent with StaticMask160).
